[SESSION CONCLUSIONS | session="BAAJA midstream top-10 ranking" | date=2026-10-09 | source=BAAJA introduced version 2026-09-30 (S.__, Capito/Lee/Whitehouse/Heinrich), docs/BAAJA_introduced_2026-09-30.txt; only version in source pack]
TOP-10 midstream provisions (ranked):
1. Bill §1202 (new CWA 401(e)-(h)): 401(g) limits NGA §7 pipeline certification to "direct point source discharge"; 9-month max clock (g)(6); 1-yr max general clock (e)(4); denial/conditions need clear & convincing evidence, burden on state in court (f); waiver if no action. Does NOT cover NGA §3 LNG terminals or non-FERC crude/NGL lines (they get only general 401(e) rules). KEY UNCERTAINTY: whether 404 dredge/fill discharges count as "direct point source discharge".
2. Bill §2102(b) (new NGA §7(i)): repair/replacement/looping/compression/capacity-enhancement of existing interstate gas pipeline & storage facilities within existing ROW/original footprint = not NEPA major federal action, not NHPA §106 undertaking. FERC §7(c) certificate, CWA, CAA, ESA still apply (§7(i)(3)). Cross-ref NEPA §3(18)(B)(xii) in Bill §1102.
3. Bill §1110 (new NEPA §111): NEPA claims filed on/after enactment: 150-day SOL (NGA 717r shorter 60-day controls), comment exhaustion, direct-harm standing, circuit-of-project exclusive jurisdiction, remedy = remand WITHOUT vacatur (180-day), authorization stays in effect and construction may continue; PI only for non-NEPA/non-NHPA violations; substantial deference. Does not limit remedies for NGA-merits (e.g., EDF v. FERC 2021 Spire) or ESA claims.
4. Bill §1204(b) (CWA 404(e)): statutorily mandated NWPs 12/14/43/57/58 (as in 91 FR 768, Jan 8 2026) for <2 acres per single & complete project; reissuance exempt from ESA §7, NHPA, NEPA EIS (programmatic EA) if preconstruction notification not narrowed; NWP term 10 yrs. Addresses Northern Plains v. Corps (D. Mont. 2020) NWP 12 vacatur. Ambiguity: whether 2-acre is ceiling or expands NWP 12 1/2-acre limit.
5. Bill §1205 (CWA 404(t)): 150-day SOL for 404 permits/NWP verifications, exhaustion, no vacatur/injunction absent imminent & substantial danger; Bill §1204(a) limits EPA 404(c) veto to application-to-issuance window (prospective).
6. Bill §1106 (NEPA §107): 1-yr EA/2-yr EIS + all other agencies decide within 90/120 days; CEQ Chair binding dispute resolution (unreviewable, deemed compliance); sponsor suit with injunctive relief, 120-day decision; no new science after NOI; alternatives must meet sponsor goals.
7. Bill §1401: bars agencies revoking/suspending/altering authorizations in effect on/after Sept 16, 2026 except court order, breach, fraud, imminent harm, or sponsor request; clear & convincing burden on agency; damages incl. 25-50% of project costs from Judgment Fund. Does not reach Presidential actions (inference; Franklin v. Massachusetts 1992) e.g., KXL 2021 permit revocation.
8. Bill §1302/§1305 (ESA): formal consultation 60 days (+ to 100), APA 706(1) relief after 145 days, consultation must finish with NEPA doc; BiOp review in D.C. Cir. within 150 days. Remedies NOT limited -> MVP-type BiOp vacatur risk (Appalachian Voices v. DOI, 4th Cir. 2022) remains. Possible conflict with NGA §19(d) (717r(d)) exclusive circuit jurisdiction.
9. Bill §2301 (NHPA §106 / 54 U.S.C. 306108): APE excludes non-federally-controlled portions; adverse effect narrowed; consultation must finish with NEPA doc; remand without vacatur; 150-day SOL; no reopen for post-initiation listings. Big for crude/NGL lines with only Corps 404/408 hooks (DAPL-type).
10. Bill §1402/§1403: disparate-treatment cause of action for listed project types (natural gas pipeline, oil pipeline, NGL pipeline, LNG export, liquefaction/regas, crude & product exports, produced water pipeline); damages 50-100% of construction cost; 1-yr decision deadline for non-NEPA authorizations (§1402(c)), enforced by §1403. Very high proof bar (intentional pattern) -> low-probability tool.
LOOKS RELEVANT BUT ISN'T: §2102(a)/FPA 216A (electric only); §2101 transmission backstop siting (electric); §1303 ESA operational ROW (MAP-21 §1316 highway CE only); §2251 OCSLA 8(p) (renewables/electric cables, not OCS oil/gas pipelines); §1402(b)(4)(D) "energy storage project" (likely not gas storage); §2211 APD on non-federal land (upstream; indirect volume effect only); §2212 tribal ROW grants (needs tribal consent, does not fix Line 5 Bad River-type disputes); §2226 pending civil actions (geothermal only); §2113 FERC fee review & §2241 staffing (administrative); §1203 NPDES 10-yr term (minor; LNG/processing plants). NOT IN BILL: CZMA §307 reform, NGA §3 LNG siting changes, NGA §7(h) eminent domain, NGA §19 judicial review, PHMSA safety, cross-border Presidential permits.
REJECTED INTERPRETATIONS: (a) that §2102(b) eliminates FERC certificate requirement — rejected, it only removes NEPA/NHPA; (b) that §1110's 150-day SOL lengthens NGA review window — rejected, "unless a shorter deadline" keeps NGA 717r 60-day; (c) that 401(g) reaches LNG terminals — rejected, text limited to NGA §7 certificates and bulk-power transmission; (d) that §1401 would have saved KXL — rejected, presidential action + Sept 16 2026 cutoff.

[ANALYSIS session=BAAJA-initial-review date=2026-10-09 doc=BAAJA introduced version (S.L.C. draft KAT26642, introduced 2026-09-30; bill no. and referral committee blank in text)]
KEY CONCLUSIONS (introduced text, 2026-09-30):
1. Structure: Div A (EPW) Title I NEPA §§1101-1133; Title II CWA §§1201-1205; Title III ESA §§1301-1308; Title IV Project Certainty §§1401-1403. Div B (ENR) Title I Transmission §§2101-2115 (incl. §2102(b) new NGA §7(i)); Title II Energy Permitting §§2201-2252 (§2201 150-day SOL; §2211 no BLM APD for <50% fed units; §2212 tribal ROWs); Title III NHPA §§2301-2302.
2. Midstream-critical: §2102(b) adds NGA §7(i): looping/compression/capacity enhancement within existing ROW or original footprint is NOT a NEPA major federal action and NOT an NHPA undertaking; CWA/CAA/other law preserved (ESA still applies). FERC certificate still needed.
3. §1202 adds CWA 401(e)-(h): scope limited to water quality requirements; denials/conditions need clear-and-convincing evidence (burden on state in court); max 1-yr review, waiver on failure to act; 401(g) NGA §7 applicants certify only 'direct point source discharge', 9-month cap. AMBIGUITY: whether a Corps 404 permit for an NGA pipeline still triggers full 401(a)(1) review (text grammatically limits 'Federal authorization or permit' clause to transmission lines).
4. §1204: 404(c) veto only between complete application and issuance (prospective, apps after enactment); NWP term 10 yrs; <2 acres per single & complete project deemed minimal; NWP 12/14/43/57/58 must be maintained; NWP reissuance exempt from ESA §7, NHPA §106 and EIS (programmatic EA) if PCN not loosened -> neutralizes Northern Plains v. Corps (2020) theory.
5. §1205/§1110/§2201/§2301(9): 150-day SOLs; remand without vacatur as default remedy (NEPA, NHPA); 404 no vacatur absent imminent & substantial danger.
6. §1106: CEQ Chair dispute-resolution orders unreviewable AND deemed full compliance with any interagency consultation/concurrence requirement in dispute (possible ESA §7 override) - highly contestable.
7. §1401: no revocation/suspension of permits 'in effect on or after Sept 16, 2026' (pre-introduction look-back date) except 5 exceptions; clear-and-convincing burden on agency; 25-50% of project costs from Judgment Fund.
8. §1402: disparate-treatment cause of action for 47 enumerated project types (incl. gas, oil, NGL, CO2, hydrogen, ammonia, produced water pipelines; LNG); damages 50-100% of expected construction cost from Judgment Fund; claims barred until 180/280 days post-enactment; pattern must post-date enactment.
9. No general effective-date section -> effective on enactment (inference). CZMA, NGA §3/DOE export, MLA §28 ROW not amended.
TOP 3 CONTESTABLE (my judgment): §1402 damages remedy; §1202 401 rewrite (federalism); §1106/§1110 CEQ unreviewable deemed-compliance + no-vacatur remedy. Runner-up: §1401 Sept 16, 2026 look-back.
REJECTED INTERPRETATIONS: (a) that §2102(b) eliminates FERC certificate need - rejected, it only addresses NEPA/NHPA status; (b) that §1305 makes D.C. Cir. exclusive venue for BiOps - rejected as unclear, text says 'may' (NGA §19(d) may still route pipeline BiOps to regional circuit); (c) that §2212 tribal ROW would have affected DAPL - rejected, Lake Oahe crossing was Corps land not tribal trust land (inference).

SEC. 1205. JUDICIAL REVIEW TIMELINE CLARITY.

 Section 404 of the Federal Water Pollution Control
Act (33 U.S.C. 1344) is amended—
 (1) in subsection (t), by striking ‘‘(t) Nothing
 in this section’’ and inserting the following:
 ‘‘(u) SAVINGS PROVISION.—Nothing in this section’’;
and
 (2) by inserting after subsection (s) the fol-
 lowing:
 ‘‘(t) JUDICIAL REVIEW.—
 ‘‘(1) STATUTE OF LIMITATIONS.—Notwith-
standing any applicable provision of law relating to
statutes of limitations—
 ‘‘(A) an action seeking judicial review,
 under subchapter II of chapter 5, and chapter
 7, of title 5, United States Code (commonly
 known as the ‘Administrative Procedure Act’),
 or any other applicable provision of law, of the
 approval by the Administrator of a State permit
 program pursuant to this section shall be filed
 not later than the date that is 150 days after
 the date on which the approval was issued, un-
 less a shorter time period is otherwise provided
 for by law;
 ‘‘(B) an action seeking judicial review,
 under subchapter II of chapter 5, and chapter
 7, of title 5, United States Code (commonly
 known as the ‘Administrative Procedure Act’),
 or any other applicable provision of law, of an
 individual permit or general permit issued
 under this section shall be filed not later than
 the date that is 150 days after the date on
 which the permit was issued, unless a shorter
 time period is otherwise provided for by law;
 and
 ‘‘(C) an action seeking judicial review,
 under subchapter II of chapter 5, and chapter
 7, of title 5, United States Code (commonly
 known as the ‘Administrative Procedure Act’),
 or any other applicable provision of law, of a
 verification that an activity involving a dis-
 charge of dredged or fill material is authorized
 by a general permit issued under this section
 shall be filed not later than the date that is 150
 days after the date on which the verification
 was issued, unless a shorter time period is oth-
 erwise provided for by law.
 ‘‘(2) LIMITATION ON COMMENCEMENT OF CER-
TAIN ACTIONS.—
 ‘‘(A) IN GENERAL.—Notwithstanding any
 other provision of law but subject to subpara-
 graph (B), no action described in subparagraph
 (A) or (B) of paragraph (1) may be commenced
 unless the action—
 ‘‘(i) is filed by a party that submitted
 a comment—
 ‘‘(I) during the public comment
 period for the administrative pro-
 ceedings related to the action; and
 ‘‘(II) that is sufficiently detailed
 to put the Administrator, the Sec-
 retary, or the State, as applicable, on
 notice of the issue on which the party
 seeks judicial review; and
 ‘‘(ii) is related to that comment.
 ‘‘(B) LIMITATION.—The limitation under
 subparagraph (A) shall only apply to actions for
 which—
 ‘‘(i) a draft of the action was pub-
 lished in the Federal Register; and
 ‘‘(ii) the applicable agency provided a
 public comment period of not less than 30
 days.
 ‘‘(3) REMEDIES FOR ACTIONS RELATING TO
PERMITS.—If a court determines that the Secretary
or a State, as applicable, did not comply with the re-
quirements of this section in issuing an individual or
general permit under this section, or in verifying
that an activity involving a discharge of dredged or
fill material is authorized by a general permit issued
under this section, or otherwise was arbitrary and
capricious under subchapter II of chapter 5, and
chapter 7, of title 5, United States Code (commonly
known as the ‘Administrative Procedure Act’), as
applicable—
 ‘‘(A) the court shall remand the matter to
 the Secretary or the State, as applicable, for
 further proceedings consistent with the deter-
 mination of the court;
 ‘‘(B) with respect to a determination re-
 garding the issuance of an individual or general
 permit under this section, the court may not va-
 cate, revoke, enjoin, or otherwise limit the per-
 mit unless the court finds that activities author-
 ized under the permit would present an immi-
 nent and substantial danger to human health or
 the environment for which there is no other eq-
 uitable remedy available under the law; and
 ‘‘(C) with respect to a determination re-
 garding a verification that an activity involving
 a discharge of dredged or fill material is au-
 thorized by a general permit issued under this
 section, the court may not enjoin or otherwise
 limit the discharge unless the court finds that
 the activity would present an imminent and
 substantial danger to human health or the envi-
 ronment for which there is no other equitable
 remedy available under the law.
 ‘‘(4) TIMELINE TO ACT ON COURT ORDER.—If
 a court remands a matter under paragraph (3), the
 court shall set and enforce a reasonable schedule
 and deadline, which may not exceed 180 days from
 the date on which the court remands the matter, ex-
 cept as otherwise required by law, for the Adminis-
 trator, the Secretary, or the State, as applicable, to
 take such actions as the court may order.’’.
 TITLE III—ENDANGERED
 SPECIES ACT OF 1973

SEC. 2243. FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

 PERSONNEL SAFETY.
 The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission may au-
thorize employees of the Federal Energy Regulatory Com-
mission to perform law enforcement duties as needed to
ensure the safety of the Chairman and Commissioners of
the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission in the per-
formance of the official duties of the Chairman and Com-
missioners, respectively.
 Subtitle F—Offshore Energy
